maya (oncall): Headline: eu-west GPU capacity degraded 10:07 UTC. Serving nodes lost connectivity to EFA fabric, autoscaler failed to provision replacements. Impact: increase in 503s for Dedicated and some Hosted routes in eu-west, traffic partially shifted to us-east automatically via smart-routing but latency spike for EU customers.

jorge (infra): Copy. I'm seeing node kernel logs showing 'nv_peer_mem: probe failed' and EFA errors. Quick dump:
```
[10:03:21] efa0: link down
[10:03:22] NVME: controller reset failed
[10:04:05] kubelet: failed to create pod sandbox: network plugin returns error
```

sami (eng-sre): Noted. Oncall runbook step 3 (scale fallback pool) didn't complete because the autoscaler IAM role returned AccessDenied for ec2:RunInstances. Looks like the temporary bursts role wasn't attached after the node group scaled down last week.

maya (oncall): we manually removed traffic from the affected AZs at 10:12 using the routing console, then increased us-east capacity. Host metrics returned to normal by ~10:40. No data loss, but several requests timed out.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback to model-v2 on hosted-prod completed at 10:30 UTC :white_check_mark:

lin (product): Heads-up from customer ops: two mid-size customers reported degraded UX, one had >30s tail latency. They were told we were failing over. Apology + timelines sent.

jorge (infra): Root causes summary we have so far: (1) EFA fabric outage in eu-west AZ affecting RDMA; (2) autoscaler role missing iam:PassRole/RunInstances so reserve pool not firing; (3) DNS TTL for smart-routing was 300s which slowed rebalancing; (4) node drain got stuck because a small number of pods used local-ssd and set terminationGracePeriod 15m.

maya (oncall): Agree. I filed PIA-4577 (post-incident action) and started a fast retrospective.

sami (eng-sre): Proposed immediate runbook updates (short list):
- Lower DNS TTL for routing records to 60s during incidents (and automated revert).
- Add preflight check to Dedicated autoscaler: verify IAM permissions for RunInstances, PassRole.
- Add explicit step to pre-warm fallback capacity in other regions when AZ-level fabric faults are detected.
- Add automated eviction helper to force-evict long-term local-ssd pods after 60s grace.

maya (oncall): Also: add a quick 'traffic-shift checklist' block with commands we used. Paste below.

jorge (infra): Good idea. Commands we actually used:
```bash
# route traffic away from eu-west AZ-A
redwood-route shift --from eu-west-az-a --to us-east --percent 100 --reason "EFA fabric failure"
# check pool sizes
kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=pool=dedicated-eu-west
# force-drain a stuck node
kubectl drain ip-10-0-5-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```

lin (product): Cost note: pre-warming fallback capacity in us-east for EU incidents will add steady-state cost if we keep it reserved — we should consider a warm pool that is spot-backed with a short startup time. Product is OK with costs for SLO-critical customers only.

maya (oncall): Action items assigned: 
- jorge: update autoscaler bootstrap to verify IAM on startup + add alert if missing (P1) — due EOD tomorrow.
- sami: edit runbook, add traffic-shift checklist and force-evict helper + create playbook test (P1) — due EOD next week.
- lin: propose product gating for paid pre-warm SLA customers and pricing note (P2) — due next Tue.
- maya: create incident postmortem draft and coordinate comms (P1) — due today.

jorge (infra): I'll also add a scheduled weekly audit that checks nodegroup IAM bindings vs expected config. If mismatch, auto-open infra-ticket.

sami (eng-sre): We should add a synthetic canary in eu-west that exercises the EFA path (small inference) every 60s and fires high-sev if failure rate > 5% for 2 minutes. That would have detected fabric degradation earlier.

maya (oncall): +1. Add to P1 runbook updates.

incident-bot: Note: Incident #2026-03-18-EU-EFA has been marked RESOLVED (severity: S3) at 10:45 UTC. Post-incident review scheduled 16:00 UTC today.

lin (product): Quick UX ask: can we add a consumer-facing status blurb that says 'traffic shifted to alternate region; some European users may see higher latency' rather than 'partial outage'? That reduces alarm.

maya (oncall): doing that now; sending message to status page and CS.

jorge (infra): Follow-ups (tech details) to include in postmortem: kernel driver versions on affected hosts, EFA firmware, nodegroup scale history, and autoscaler logs between 09:50-10:20. I'll attach them to the PIA.

sami (eng-sre): Also adding test cases for the runbook: simulate EFA failure in staging by toggling the virtual NIC and ensure automated traffic-shift completes within 90s.

maya (oncall): Thanks all. We'll review the draft postmortem at 16:00 and lock down the runbook edits after sign-off.

lin (product): Appreciated. Customers want SLA clarity; let's ensure the product gating language is tight.

jorge (infra): One last note: consider reducing our cross-region warmup time by snapshotting AMIs with pre-pulled model weights to cut node bootstrap from ~7m to ~90s. That reduces failover costs/latency.

maya (oncall): added to P2 ideas but useful for ops optimization.

sami (eng-sre): I'll draft the runbook diff and post as PR to infra/runbooks in ~2 hours.

maya (oncall): Closing thread for now — will reopen if anything else pops up. :hand:
